Znowu, jak w wielu innych przypadkach, wolałbym, żeby istniał jakiś złoty środek, a nie tylko binarne „tak” lub „nie”. Ale do dzieła. Jest kilka fajnych rzeczy. Duży potencjał. Potem zakończenie, które było brutalnym momentem, który bez wahania zasłużył na minus. Przejdźmy do konkretów.

Zalety
To tania gra. Czas rozgrywki nie jest długi, ale grałem chyba 5,6 godziny i myślę, że gra była warta swojej ceny aż do ostatniej minuty. Był tu duży potencjał. Czułem, że to nowsza wersja czegoś w stylu Hardspace: Shipbreaker. Potencjał jest. Rozwijaj się, spłacaj długi, kontynuuj jazdę. Gra była bardzo spokojna i nie musiałem się zbytnio stresować. Widziałem potencjał na końcówkę gry, gdzie możesz skończyć z jakimś wygenerowanym systemem, zapłacić za roszczenie do jednego z nich i zacząć go wydobywać dla zysku. Nie mogłem się doczekać, dokąd to doprowadzi. W grze jest mnóstwo opcji. Czy chcę wiercić, czy po prostu wysadzać rzeczy w powietrze? Daje ci to opcje, jak chcesz rozwiązać sytuację.

Złe
Ciągłe klikanie myszką. Teraz możesz przytrzymać przycisk, żeby kopać, tak, ale kopanie odbywa się o połowę wolniej niż przy klikaniu. Nie rozumiem, jak można było tego nie zaprogramować, żeby po prostu szybko kopać, trzymając myszkę. Dobra opcja, która powinna się tam znaleźć. Inną irytującą cechą jest to, że na początku gry, dopóki nie osiągniesz większej pojemności tlenu, ciągle słyszysz ten komunikat o niskim poziomie tlenu. Jasne, ostrzega cię i to dobrze, ale na początku gry masz tak mało tlenu, że kichasz, kończy ci się tlen i znowu słyszysz ostrzeżenie. Daj mi chociaż seksowny głos, żebym mógł go słuchać, jeśli zamierzasz mnie nim atakować w kółko.

Brzydkie
Ostatnie kilka minut gry. To była fajna i relaksująca jazda aż do tego momentu, a twórcy gry dali nam popalić. Wydało mi się to irytujące, chamskie i banalne, po prostu mnie zdołowało. Nie będę zdradzał szczegółów, ale pomyślałem sobie... „Wow, właśnie zmarnowałem 6 godzin mojego życia”. Wszystko, co zrobiłem i zbudowałem, poszło dosłownie na marne, w ramach z góry zaplanowanego i zaplanowanego ruchu, który przypominał coś, co robi pewna firma, która uwielbia tworzyć gry o zabójcach.

Podsumowanie
Nie mogę polecić tej gry. Ma kilka zalet. Mnóstwo możliwości, żeby kiedyś udekorować swój statek, zdobyć inny, może zobaczyć mapy sterowane proceduralnie. Ale sposób, w jaki się skończyło, bez żadnej kontroli czy głosu z mojej strony, sprawia, że ​​daję jej kciuk w dół. Nie wierzcie mi jednak na słowo. Ale na końcu będziecie chcieli też trzepnąć kozę. Słabi twórcy, źli.
Jasna podróbka Digging A Hole. Czy to całe „Kop, biegnij z powrotem, żeby sprzedać, kop dalej, biegnij z powrotem, żeby sprzedać, ulepsz swoją małą łopatę do większej”, a nawet daje wiertło jako narzędzie do kopania na końcu gry i robi to samo: „Koniec gry to twoja śmierć bez żadnego sensownego zakończenia”.

Gra zawiera mnóstwo treści, które były wyraźnie zaplanowane, ale nigdy nie zostały zaimplementowane, w tym dwa pomieszczenia na statku (i dwa włazy na górze i na dole), które nic nie robią i nigdy nie robią, lokacje, o których twórcy stwierdzili, że „nie są interesujące” i zostaną usunięte, więc i tak nie można się do nich dostać, oraz okna dialogowe, które wspominają o rzeczach długo po ich znalezieniu, bez realnego sposobu na ich rozwiązanie.

Zaoszczędź pięć dolców i czas poświęcony na grindowanie. Kup dosłownie cokolwiek innego.
Najlepiej, co mogę powiedzieć? Prawie warte swojej ceny. Gra trwa około 5 godzin i kończy się niesamowicie niesatysfakcjonującym zakończeniem. Jest niedokończona i nie ma dowodów na to, że kiedykolwiek będzie. Czy wspominałem już, że zakończenie jest niesatysfakcjonujące? Krzyczy też, że zabrakło im pomysłów na dalszą część i postanowili obtoczyć to gówno w brokacie, żeby wyglądało trochę lepiej.

Ogółem? Biorąc pod uwagę, jak gra się kończy? (Giniesz, postrzelony od tyłu, przez kogoś, kto wyskakuje znikąd, wyrwany z kontekstu) i GDZIE się kończy? (stacja położona pośrodku asteroidy/małej planety, którą musisz wykopać?) i że w HUD statku kosmicznego są odniesienia do dalszych lokacji i sektorów???

1) Баги. Их не так много, но они есть. Те, с которыми я столкнулась: попадание в текстуры, что телепортирует тебя обратно на корабль со словами в духе "блин, надеюсь скоро этот известный баг починят!" и баг с тем, что не можешь телепортироваться в нужную точку.

Overall: Great gameplay, confusing upgrades, stupid AI art in some places, cool story. I would change my rating if the art was not AI generated.

Gameplay: Starts off as annoying (albeit funny with a spoon) and steadily iterates to become more productive. Easily the best part of the game, especially finding the secrets everywhere. The upgrade tree feels super unbalanced at times, however, that almost never takes away from the fun of it.

Art: Generally okay overall, but the obvious use of AI really robs enjoyment from the style of the game. The music is cute and campy, but the pictures of the boss and Grandpa really makes it feel like an asset flip style game. I HEAVILY recommend spending some money to update the game with more stylized artwork.

Story: Interesting in some spots, seems slapped together in other spots. It is interesting enough to read all of the dialogue and understand the motivation of your character. I feel like the story itself would be way more impactful if they used voice actors. Not a complaint, but it would add a lot to the vibe of the game.

Ich habe das Spiel jetzt nach ca. 10 Stunden gemütlicher Spielzeit beendet und es hat mich echt positiv Überrascht. Wer ein richtig cooles Indie-Game zum Abschalten für's Wochenende sucht, ist hier an der exakt richtigen Adresse.

Im Spiel schlüpft man in die Rolle eines intergalaktischen Schatzsuchers. Zu Beginn erbt man ein altes Raumschiff von seinem Großvater (quasi ein unfreiwillig aufgezwungenes Erbe) und reist dann aus der Ego-Perspektive quer durch eine offene Galaxie. Das große Ziel ist es, die verstreuten Fragmente eines uralten Artefakts „Herz der Leere“ zu finden und das Relikt wieder zusammenzusetzen. Dafür klappert man verschiedene Asteroiden ab, farmt wertvolle Ressourcen, verkauft das Zeug und rüstet damit Stück für Stück seine Ausrüstung auf.

Es gibt Anfangs kein Tutorial, was es aber auch überhaupt nicht braucht, weil sich das Spiel quasi komplett von selbst erklärt. So wie die meisten Digging a Hole spiele. Die Story rund um die Suche nach dem Artefakt und diesen Gravitex-Konzern ist richtig cool aufgezogen und der Humor dabei trifft genau meinen Geschmack.

Auch optisch macht es wirklich was her. Die Weltraum-Vibes kommen super rüber, die Grafik ist wunderschön gestaltet und was die Performance angeht, läuft das Spiel an sich butterweich und ohne Probleme.
Naja... fast ohne Probleme. Das Einzige, was die FPS wirklich mal gepflegt in die Knie zwingt, ist das letzte Level. Wenn man da anfängt, mit der Mini-Atombombe rumzuschmeißen und plötzlich knappe 5.000 Items gleichzeitig quer über den Bildschirm fliegen, fängt der PC schon kurz an zu schwitzen. Aber ganz ehrlich, das ist eigentlich fast schon wieder witzig und wenn man das weiß, ist es absolut kein Drama.

Für den Preis ist der Gesamteindruck eigentlich wirklich super und ein Bonus am Ende ist auch noch dabei. Geiler Gameplay-Loop, entspannte Atmosphäre und eine schöne Welt. Von mir gibt's eine ganz klare Empfehlung und einen Daumen nach oben!

[h3]掘り99%以上わずかにパズルや推理というゲーム[/h3]
このゲーム構成上、ただひたすら掘りたい人にとっては90点以上のゲームとなるかも？というゲームです。
万人受けするかというとちょっと微妙かもしれません。
個人的にはお値段分以上には楽しみました。全ゲーム要素クリアー済み、実績全解除状態までプレイしています。


[u][b]良い点[/b][/u]
・基本は掘りです。シンプルに掘りたいためにゲームをする人にとっては最高でしょう。その気があれば永久に掘れるシステムになっています。
・宇宙空間の無重力・無酸素状態で掘るのが基本で、その点は興味深いです。一方で重力下の掘りもあり、攻略方法が異なるので面白いところです。
・個人的には楽しみましたが、掘りと関係がないパズルや推理する部分は、掘りたい人がやるはずのこのゲームでは賛否分かれそうです。自分は良いアクセントで気分転換にもなりました。
・セール中に買えばワンコイン以下ですが、攻略手順やどこまで掘り尽くしていくかにもよりますが丸一日以上は遊べるボリュームのはずです。本編クリアーの目安は15時間～程度かなと思われ、非常にリーズナブルで良いと思います。
・仮にちょっとダレてきたとしても、すぐにゲームを中断して、再開可能な仕組みになっています。自分は一気にクリアーしてしまいましたが、ちょっとずつ遊ぶにも向いています。
・ローカライズは悪くはなさそうですが、意味が取りにくいと感じる部分があり、あとわざとなのかな？という変な翻訳があります。ただ、意味は分かりますので、プレイに支障はないと思います。
・掘り世界を渡り歩いてきていて、とても掘り慣れている人にとって、あれ？このステージの構造・造形は・・・と、ニヤリとするステージが登場しますので、それを楽しみにしていてください。
・グラフィックは綺麗です。デフォルメされていますが、自分は好印象でした。


[u][b]悪い点[/b][/u]
・攻略面含め、ゲームの性質を掴むまで、ちょっとペースが悪いように感じるかもしれません。それもゲーム性といえばそうなんですが、もしかするとそこで人が離れるかもしれません。
・セーブもロードも、ゲーム内のオブジェクト数依存だと思われ、モノが多いステージになるととんでもなく時間を要します。仕方ない面もありますが、一見してフリーズして見えることもあり、上手く圧縮する方法が必要に思えます。あるいはセーブとロードの前処理にもプログレスバーをつけて、フリーズに見せない工夫は必要だと思います。
・掘る能力が低いと、掘りで引っかかりやすいのと、ゴミが残りやすいのが気になりました。ゴミが出るとその後の掃除が難しいことも多く発生し、場合によっては明らかにヒットしていてもゴミが消えなかったりもして、気持ち悪かったです。どうにかする方法が欲しいところです。特に重力下で中空に残るゴミは凶悪です。
・上記と関係しますが、一度綺麗に掘りつくして採りつくしたところに、ゴミや資源が復活していることがあります。ロード後に多いようですが、見た目の処理と内部のオブジェクトデータの処理に齟齬（=バグ）がありそうです。

Decent little game, it was fun and satisfying and it plays it pretty safe as far as these type of incremental games go. It's pretty simple and straightforward so it doesn't over-stay its welcome, but at the same time the art direction leaves a lot to be desired. The UI was servicable at best and the character movement in zero-g and environmental interaction felt somewhat unpolished. The upgrade tree didn't have a lot of variety and satisfaction. Most of that was to be had getting bigger numbers by collecting more ore and digging up hidden caches using your radar, which was still fun. There's not a lot of SFX or ambience and there's virtually no music as well, so the game sort of feels flat. To cap that off, I really didn't like the AI portraits. It left me wondering where else AI has left its fingerprint on this game and ultimately breaks trust even if there's nowhere else and the description is true. Just an image of two different in-game space-suits would do better than what's currently in place if commissioning an artist was too expensive. I can forgive an indie game for not having the strongest artistic direction or presentation, but it's really tough to recommend this game due to the use of AI. There are better incremental games, and certainly better digging games, but this is still fun and I would still recommend it if you've exhausted a lot of your other mining media.

Pros:
- Mechanics / Physics work well
- Leveling up your equipment has a good pace
- New tools found on digs are actually very useful
- Background music just works for this game
- Decent storyline progression
- And a fun addition of some mini-games on the wall of the ship

Cons:
- In bigger asteroids you go into, it's sometime overly difficult to get out because there may be a tiny leftover piece you need to harvest out of the way and it prevents you from escaping... then you die because... oxygen.
- Not really a con, but the devs need to run their story lines through spellcheck as there are many misspelled words. Again, this is more for fine tuning the game... not so much a con of game-play itself.

DGT is a space mining and loot game with an affordable price point, and I seldom encountered optimization issues whatsoever.
Since there’s no automation feature, it requires a amount of grinding. The game introduces exploring and puzzle solving — I did get stuck for a while, I was able to finish the game and unlock all achievements in roughly 12 hours overall.
Naturally, the game isn’t without its flaws, but the devs have been proactive in releasing fixes and updates. That’s quite commendable for a small indie game.

Digger: Galactic Treasures is a charming and relaxing space-mining adventure that captures the nostalgic spirit of classic digging games while giving it a cosmic twist. Developed and published by RainStyle Games, it places players in the role of a lone prospector navigating a galaxy filled with mystery, greed, and hidden riches. The story is light but effective, framing the player as a small-time scavenger who inherits an old mining ship and sets out to uncover lost relics and rare minerals scattered across forgotten planets and asteroids. The universe is ruled by corporate powers that have stripped most of the easy resources, leaving only danger and discovery for independent miners brave enough to venture beyond the regulated sectors. It’s a familiar setup, but the tone leans toward curiosity and wonder rather than cynicism, giving the game an optimistic flavor that fits well with its relaxed gameplay rhythm.

The gameplay loop centers on exploration and gradual progression, drawing players into a satisfying cycle of excavation, upgrading, and discovery. At its core, the experience revolves around mining asteroid fields and planetary surfaces for valuable ores and artifacts. Each new location feels like an isolated puzzle waiting to be unraveled as you carve paths through rock and uncover shimmering veins of resources. These materials can be sold or refined to improve your ship’s equipment, unlock new areas, and expand your range of operations. Progress is steady and rewarding, the kind of incremental advancement that makes every session feel meaningful. The early stages are slow, with modest tools and limited energy reserves forcing players to plan their dives carefully, but the eventual sense of empowerment that comes from building a more capable ship makes the journey worth it.

What keeps the experience engaging is the way it balances simplicity with atmosphere. The environments may be procedurally structured, but each has a distinct sense of place thanks to thoughtful lighting, color palettes, and ambient effects. The visuals lean into a soft, stylized realism that makes asteroids and alien landscapes feel tangible without overwhelming detail. The music complements this perfectly—calm, spacey tones that make mining feel less like labor and more like quiet meditation. The sound design adds another layer of immersion: the hum of drills, the echo of explosions in hollow caverns, and the gentle clinking of minerals hitting your cargo bay all reinforce the sensation of solitude in the void. There’s something soothing about being alone among the stars, guided only by the soft glow of your ship’s instruments and the promise of treasure buried deep beneath the surface.

As your skills and equipment improve, the game begins to reveal its broader narrative threads. Ancient ruins, strange relics, and encrypted data logs hint at a galactic mystery involving a long-lost artifact known as the Heart of the Void. These discoveries add texture to the world without disrupting the flow of play. The story unfolds gradually through environmental storytelling and small narrative fragments, which makes the universe feel larger than the player’s small corner of it. The sense of isolation is counterbalanced by curiosity—each find teases at something greater, a secret hidden in the stars. This structure ensures that the game remains more than a mechanical loop of mining and upgrading; it offers a quiet sense of purpose, an overarching mystery that drives you forward without resorting to heavy exposition or cinematic sequences.

Despite its many strengths, Digger: Galactic Treasures is still a modest indie project, and its limitations are easy to spot. The game’s short length and somewhat abrupt ending leave a lingering feeling that there could have been more to uncover. The upgrade paths, while satisfying, eventually plateau, and once you’ve fully optimized your ship, the incentive to continue digging diminishes. Some players may find the pace too slow, especially early on, as progress requires patience and repetition. Technical performance, on the other hand, is solid across the board—the game runs smoothly on both desktop and handheld systems, including the Steam Deck, which makes it ideal for short, relaxing play sessions. Its lightweight nature and intuitive controls also make it accessible to casual players, and its low system requirements ensure that nearly anyone can enjoy it.

Community reception has been strongly positive, and for good reason. Players consistently praise its relaxing atmosphere, well-tuned controls, and satisfying sense of progression. Many describe it as the perfect game to unwind with—a quiet, meditative escape into space where the only real pressure comes from how deep you’re willing to dig. Its approachable design, coupled with a fair price, makes it an easy recommendation for fans of exploration and resource-management games. While it doesn’t push boundaries or reinvent the genre, it succeeds in delivering exactly what it promises: a compact, enjoyable experience built on simple mechanics and a tranquil sci-fi aesthetic.

Digger: Galactic Treasures works because it understands its own scale. It doesn’t try to be a sprawling space epic or a complex management simulator. Instead, it focuses on the elemental satisfaction of discovery, the small joys of progress, and the allure of uncovering something ancient and valuable hidden in the dark. Its combination of calm pacing, gentle storytelling, and tactile gameplay gives it a warmth rarely found in space exploration titles. The result is a game that feels like both an adventure and a meditation—a reminder that sometimes the greatest treasures aren’t in what you find, but in the quiet, deliberate act of searching.

Just wrapped it up, and overall I’d say the game is good but feels more like a beta — there’s a solid foundation here, but it’s still missing a lot of depth and polish. The story starts off strong, but it fades a bit as you go, and some areas of the ship are just empty rooms, which makes things feel unfinished.

I was expecting something more exploration and resource-driven, like visiting randomly generated planets to gather materials for ship and gear upgrades — for example, needing copper or iron for better tools, or unlocking new, more profitable (and more dangerous) destinations. That kind of system would’ve added longevity and replayability, especially if areas could reset or randomize over time while keeping story zones persistent.

A few small issues stood out too:
- The vacuum feels weak — would love an upgrade path for its suction power.
- Energy drains way too fast, even at max level.
- And seriously, let us buy bombs! Would’ve added a lot of fun and chaos to planetary runs.

Despite the rough edges, I do like the core gameplay and the potential here. If the devs keep updating it and flesh out the story and systems, this could turn into something really special. For now, it’s an interesting but incomplete experience that I hope continues to grow.

The graphics and mechanics, for the most part, are pretty sound. Every now and then it'll throw a bug or choppy slowdown your way, but it's fairly rare. As for the gameplay loop, well, it's boring, but that's kind of the point. Basically you mine asteroids for materials, sell those materials to earn credits, use those credits to upgrade your equipment to mine faster. Repeat. And repeat. And repeat. Just settle in for a couple hours of repeating. It took me 10 hours to 100% the game but in hindsight, I could have probably done it in half the time had I been focused on the right things in the beginning.

Now that may not sound like a glowing review, but I actually enjoyed it. Sometimes you just need a brainless grind. Maybe you had a rough week at work, maybe you're coming off a much more complicated game and you don't want to spend a week in the learning curve, etc. I can just sit down for a couple hours of grinding, but chill grinding, kinda like a zen garden. 

The progression of how fast you can obtain materials is also kind of addicting. You start out very slow and it builds and it gets pretty exciting towards the end with how much you can grab at once.

I think as long as you know what you're getting into and don't expect more than that from it, you'll actually really like it. It may be simple, but it's a polished simple. I really hope the developers use this as a springboard to make more complex games because I think they'd do well (and be sure to hire an English localization person lol).

У меня две новости. Первая плохая, вторая... тоже плохая.

Во-первых, наш дедушка умер. 

Во-вторых, он оставил нам свой старый полураздолбанный пепелац. В смысле, космический корабль. В общем, нам придётся отработать долг. И заодно найти то, что нашёл наш дед. Нашёл, а потом заботливо припрятал в одном из астероидов. От греха подальше.

[h1][b] Где-то там, в космосе, есть планета без войн, без насилия, без голода и бедности, без убийств и без зла, без воды и без кислорода [/b][/h1]
Итак, у нас есть корабль, система с несколькими небольшими астероидами и ложка. Натуральная столовая ложка, которой и придётся копать.

Геймплей прост, как три рубля. 

Покидаем корабль, подлетаем к астероиду, зажимаем ЛКМ. Всё, ложка копает, мы собираем руду. 

Поначалу это тот ещё геморрой. Кислорода мало, копается медленно, единица железной руды стоит одну деньгу. Так долг не отработаешь. 

Но, как известно, терпение и труд всё перетрут! Вскоре мы получим лопату, потом кирку и наконец отбойник. А ещё есть сборщик, взрывчатка, телепорт и разные улучшения типа увеличения кислорода, инвентаря и скорости передвижения. Да и руды будут куда дороже. 

Время от времени внутри раскапываемых астероидов мы будем находить сейфы с деньгами и полезными девайсами. А ещё разный хлам (читай - артефакты), на который можно полюбоваться на корабле в своеобразном мини-музее.

Перемещение на корабле по сектору Х происходит следующим образом. Мы выкапываем необходимое для закрытия локации количество руды. Например, в первом секторе это будут пять кусков меди. Видим на мониторе надпись "Сектор закрыт на 100%", идём на капитанский мостик, выбираем следующую локацию и прыгаем к месту назначения.

Also there is a hatch on the floor and ceiling of the ship that say "Closed".  And the Corp who gives you your assignments talks about getting you access to another sector of space, but you never get that access.  So I am wondering if the Devs will have some kind of content update that will add additional sectors as well as utilizing the empty rooms on the ship. 

As it sit right now, the game is about 4-6 hours of content, and for $5 (less than a coffee) I think it was worth it.  I know I feel like I got my $5 worth. Digger: Galactic Treasures is a thrilling and charming arcade-style digging adventure that perfectly blends classic gameplay with modern polish. This game takes the nostalgic fun of retro dig-and-collect titles and injects it with colorful sci-fi themes, fast-paced action, and plenty of strategic depth—making it a must-play for fans of classic arcade games and casual action alike.

The gameplay is straightforward but highly engaging: you dig through layers of alien soil to uncover valuable treasures while avoiding traps, enemies, and environmental hazards. The controls feel tight and responsive, allowing for smooth navigation through complex underground mazes. Collecting resources and power-ups adds layers of strategy, encouraging players to plan their digging routes carefully to maximize rewards and survival.

Visually, Digger: Galactic Treasures shines with bright, cartoonish graphics and fun sci-fi flair. The colorful planets and quirky alien creatures make exploration exciting, and the sound design perfectly complements the arcade vibe with upbeat tunes and satisfying effects.

What really makes the game stand out is its balance of challenge and accessibility. It’s easy to pick up and enjoy in short bursts but offers enough variety and progression to keep you hooked longer. Whether you’re competing for high scores or simply exploring new levels, the game’s pacing and design feel just right.

Why I Recommend It:
Digger: Galactic Treasures is a fantastic blend of old-school arcade charm and fresh, colorful sci-fi adventure. If you love digging games, fast-paced action, or just want a fun, casual experience that’s easy to jump into but hard to put down, this game delivers on all fronts. It’s a delightful blast from the past with a modern twist—definitely worth digging into!

[h3] 前言 [/h3]
 不知道各位是否喜欢那种挖掘或切割东西时发出“莎莎”的声音，通常可以在各类解压视频里听到，大部分人平时可能没什么机会去亲手制造这种声音，但在本作，玩家有着一个赛博机会。
[h3] 背景介绍 [/h3]
 恭喜你，成功继承了你祖父的一切财产，包括一艘传奇老船，和无数的资产——负债资产。
现在公司决定派遣你去挖掘些值钱的东西，但由于你欠款过多，公司无法发放挖掘设备，不过好在，公司还是给你准备了一个工具：一根塑料勺子，好了别抱怨了，用这个勺子去把小行星挖穿吧！
[h3] 游玩建议 [/h3]
 本作的流程属于经典滚雪球的玩法，早期起步很难，但随着阶段进行收益会越来越高，数值越滚越大，爽感随之而来，在这里建议优先升级挖掘设备，不然会非常坐牢，其次，善用扫描设备，本作的挖掘是有指标的，虽然后期玩家的工具足够强大，可以1随意挖掘，但前期靠一个勺子简直寸步难行，建议根据扫描器优先完成任务升级挖掘工具后再资源探索。

优秀的挖掘手感，发出的白噪音非常舒适，非常解压
[*]优点2
比较舒服的流程设计，除了在最早期有一点牢以外，其他时间段的体验都很丝滑。
[*]缺点1 
质量极差的机翻，credit，在这里应该是信用点的意思，结果在中文里翻译成制作人员了。 
 
[h3] 个人感受 [/h3]
由于机翻，游戏刚开始的时候我没看懂提示的意思，拿着一个破勺子挖了半天，解压没怎么解，倒是增压了不少。
不过在理解扫描器怎么使用后，快速获取第一桶金并升级了勺子，往后的流程就非常简单且爽了，总的来说非常推荐！

I'm updating my previous review based on recent updates. While I would still say that this is still basically A Game About Digging A Hole : in space, that wasn't why I originally didn't recommend it in my first review. On release, while it was presented as a 1.0 version, the story was obviously incomplete and the "ending" was even more unsatisfying than the ending of AGADAH. The dev did respond to my review after dropping an update or two, and with the pace of further updates and patches, it doesn't feel like a drop and run game anymore. I am working on a second play-through, so at least until I complete that, I am changing my review to positive. 

Note to the developer: While I understand that it may be difficult to release in Early Access and get traction, the state of the game was almost exactly what EA is meant for. You had good bones, a decent game-play loop, and at least enough of a story to get me interested in seeing where it goes. Unfortunately, the "ending" was a sucker punch after taking the time to carefully go through each level and putting about 13 hours into it. If it had been an EA release, or even if the fade to black had a small disclaimer that you were still working on finishing the story, my first review would have been positive. When you put "1.0" on your version, that should mean that even if you have more you want to add, you would be OK with the state of the game [i]as is[/i] being your legacy if something happened where you were unable to continue development for whatever reason. 
Also, I'm not sure what your first language is, and I can't pull up your dev page while writing the review, but some (most) of the text conversations are pretty difficult to read (in English). While I'm not bilingual, I'm sure you could find someone in your community who is that would be willing to help clean up the translations. If nothing else, I would be willing to act as an English editor, cleaning up the exposition and making it more natural sounding for the English speaking audience, at least. I do believe you have a game with good potential, and I hope you keep developing it, and I will follow you to see what you come up with next. Good Luck!

[b]Вывод:[/b]
“[b]Digger: Galactic Treasures[/b]” - небольшой фан-проект от русскоязычной команды [b]RainStyle Games[/b], ранее отметившейся весьма эксцентричной аркадой “[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1443630/?snr=1_5_9__412]Turbo Sloths[/url]”, в которой ленивцы гоняют на спортивных асфальтоукладчиках. На этот раз разработчики решили сбавить обороты и создали так называемый [b]cozy[/b]-[b]relax[/b] проект, где игроку предстоит расслабляться... под монотонную, почти медитативную работу космического шахтера.

Проект вдохновлен, как ни странно, другой российской игрой - “[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/738520/Breathedge/]Breathedge[/url]”. Поэтому если Вы с ней знакомы, приготовьтесь ловить отсылки, параллели и знакомые мотивы - от визуальных гэгов до общей атмосферы “злого абсурда”.

Вы - обычный рабочий, обитающий на станции “Калифорния-15”. Внезапно узнаете о пропаже своего деда (ну а как иначе?) и по завещанию получаете его ветхий корабль “[b]Lumen-17[/b]” - вместе с солидным долгом перед добывающей корпорацией “[b]GRAVEX[/b]”. Другими словами - добро пожаловать в жизнь раба корпорации.

Ваш выбор прост: либо работать на “[b]GRAVEX[/b]”, копая космическую пыль, либо... впрочем, другого пути и не предусмотрено. А чтобы совсем стало весело, во время одной из вылазок Ваш старенький дедовский радар внезапно активируется и передает запись: дед, оказывается, нашел артефакт, способный создавать целые миры! И теперь за ним охотится корпорация. Ваша цель - не просто расплатиться с долгами, а найти артефакт раньше злодеев в галстуках. В идеале - еще и спасти галактику, попутно выяснив, во что вообще вляпался Ваш предок. 

Как несложно догадаться, основа геймплея - это... копание. Много копания. Исследуйте астероиды, метеориты и другие небесные камни, добывайте ресурсы, продавайте их, улучшайте снаряжение и возвращайтесь в “бой” с новым оборудованием.

Игра буквально начинается с “пластиковой ложки” - Ваше первое оборудование настолько беспомощно, что даже гречку с тарелки руками соскрести будет проще. Музыка здесь - редкий гость. Хотя, быть может, к тому моменту Вам уже будет уютно в этой тишине. Несмотря на то, что игра сделана на [b]Unreal Engine 5[/b], ни [b]Lumen[/b], ни [b]RTX[/b] тут не активированы - и слава пиксельному богу. Это сильно разгружает систему. Однако! Поэтому крайне рекомендую устанавливать игру на [b]SSD[/b]. Иначе есть шанс столкнуться с визуальной “пустотой” - когда Вы уже выкопали кусок астероида, а текстура еще не подгрузилась. Мелочь, но именно такие штуки могут особенно раздражать впечатлительных эстетов, которые требуют от игры за 72 рубля визуального лоска уровня “[b]Star Citizen[/b]”

Es gab ja ein paar "Digging" Spiele. Also wo man Löcher graben und Erze finden muss, diese verkaufen, sein EQ zu verbessern, um noch mehr und noch tiefer zu graben. Dieses Spiel hier ist das gleiche Prinzip, nur halt im Weltall. Es gibt ca. halbes Dutzend Orte, die wir abgrasen bzw. abbauen müssen. Zwar sehen die vom Aussehen gleich aus, aber die Kometen werden immer größer und manche haben sogar eine Schwerkraft - ansonsten schwebt man ganze Zeit nur.

Man fängt mit einem Löffel an und arbeitet sich von Spitzhacke zu Erdbohrer hin, der immer wieder Energie braucht. Im All benötigen wir Sauerstoff, der uns Anfangs glaube kaum 30 Sekunden am Leben hält und man so immer wieder frühzeitig zum Schiff muss, das kostet auch Zeit. Somit hat man kaum 20 Sekunden Anfangs zum Abbauen. Stirbt man, landet man auf sein Schiff, nichts weiter passiert, außer, dass die gesammelten Ressourcen weg sind.

Als Hilfsmittel gibt es Lichter, Bomben, Teleport und Sauerstoffstation etc. bis auf die Bomben kann man die Sachen auch kaufen. Ansonsten findet man immer wieder solche Tresore, die einige Gegenstände u.a. Bomben enthalten. 

Man gräbt sich also in die Kometen oder was es sein soll hinein, sammelt Erze von Eisen/Kupfer bis später zu Gold/Diamanten/Titan etc. diese verkaufen wir und bekommen Geld, die wir wiederum in Ausrüstung bzw. Skills wie mehr Sauerstoff oder mehr Inventar etc. ausgeben können.

Zwischen den ganzen Chaos können wir auch noch Artefakte finden, die dann im Raumschiff herumliegen, wobei ich mich frage, wo die letzten 6-7 sind, die ich noch zwecks eines Erfolgs sammeln musste... Mh.

Ansonsten gibt es hier nur hin und wieder Textnachrichten, die uns irgendwie eine kleine Geschichte erzählen soll. Wir können nur zum nächsten Ort Reisen, wenn wir den Sektor zu 100% fertig gesammelt haben. Das heißt nicht, alles zerstören und sammeln, sondern nur bestimmte Sachen, die auch unser Radar anzeigt. Es ist aber immer Ratsam alles zu zerstören, da es Ressourcen gibt, die uns Geld bringen.

Abzüglich Idle Zeit hab ich etwa 20-22 Stunden für 100% gebraucht. Alleine der "Würfelplanet" hat mich sehr sehr viele Stunden gekostet. Würde man auf den keine einzige voll ausgebaute Bombe werfen, würde man 20+ Stunden brauchen :D

Kleiner Nachteile waren z.B. 
- Dass man immer wieder seine Lichter abgebaut oder sie mit dem Sauger aufgesaugt hat. Das sollte man ändern. Licht sollte sich mit 3-5 Sekunden festhalten einer Taste abbauen lassen
- Zudem fehlte mir eine Kopflampe. Es ist häufig sooo Dunkel und die Lichter bringen ja nichts, wenn du da um dich herum abbaust. Dann baust du die Lampe wieder ab... und so wie ich sah, gab es keine Helligkeitseinstellung
- Es gibt nichts zu entdecken außer Ressourcen, Tresore und Artefakte
- So gut wie keine wirkliche Story vorhanden
- Die "Orte" sahen fast immer 1zu1 gleich aus
- Im Raumschiff gibt es Zimmer, die total leer sind - warum eigentlich?
- Der Letzte Ort hat ein paar Lagg Probleme, wahrscheinlich wegen zu viel Ressourcen

Fazit: Mir hat es trotzdem sehr viel Spaß gemacht, hab Nebenbei immer Dokus oder Serien geschaut. Wir brauchen mehr solcher Spiele, aber mit etwas mehr Inhalt bzw. mehr Motivation. Ich liebe solche Graben-Spiele :)

[h1]宇宙で繰り広げられる定番掘削ゲーム[/h1]
　隕石/小惑星から鉱石を回収し換金、自身の装備を強化してくというよくある掘削ゲーム。ゲームシステム自体は既存のものと比べて遜色ないですが、隕石から小惑星へとステージがスケールアップしていく進行による、成長の実感と掘削の爽快感がしっかりと味わえる作りになっているのは好印象でした。
　また、各ステージには収集要素として「アーティファクト」が隠されており、それらを探すのも小さな楽しみの一つです。恐らく他作品のオマージュ的なアイテムが多かったのかなと思うのですが、私はあまりピンと来ませんでした...笑。とはいえ、鉱石掘削とは別の目標があることで探索の幅が広がっていたと感じます。

[h2]後半の単調さと重力ステージのストレスが惜しい[/h2]
　前半～中盤にかけては「掘削→換金→装備強化」というゲームサイクルがしっかりと機能していたものの、中盤で装備がほぼ完成してしまい、後半は鉱石を集める目的が曖昧になりました。更に装備のインフレにより爆弾やエネルギーなどが実質使い放題となり、ゲーム性はお掃除ゲーへと変貌していきます。その結果、装備強化のワクワク感が薄れ、徐々に作業感が増していくのが勿体なかったです。
　また、惑星に重力があるステージでは、どこに向かって移動しているのかが分かりづらく、操作が思い通りにいかないストレスが頻発しました。無重力ステージではそれが一切なかったため、重力を導入するのであれば、もう少し操作性をあげてほしかったです。

ゲームとしての基礎は堅実で、宇宙掘削という舞台設定や収集要素も魅力的。ただし後半の単調さと操作性のストレスが目立つため、序盤の面白さを最後まで保てていたら、もっと人にオススメしたくなるゲームだったかもしれません。
[hr]
[h2]2025/09/03「氷の惑星」アップデート[/h2]
　新要素として追加されたのは新たなアーティファクト、ツルハシ&爆弾の新アップグレードです。ただ正直個人的には"ドリル"のアップグレードが欲しかったところ。ツルハシは探索範囲が広くなったとはいえ、やはりテンポ感に欠けると感じます。爆弾の強化で破壊範囲が脅威の2倍となっていますが、取得できるタイミングが氷の惑星内部の施設でほぼ探索を終えた後なのも惜しいところです。次回へのアップデートへの布石という印象が強いです。

[h2]掘削の原点から少し外れた方向性[/h2]
　本編終盤あたりから感じていたことですが、私は"鉱石堀り"をしたいのであって、"遺跡のような建造物を掘り当てたい"訳ではないんですよね。氷の惑星内部にも謎の施設が埋まっており、その入口を探すために広大な範囲をひたすら岩を削って回るという地味な作業が続きます。序盤の「掘って稼いで強化していく」という爽快なテンポ感とはかけ離れたゲーム性になっているように感じます。

[hr]
[h1]2025/10/30「古い天文台」アップデート[/h1]
　今回のアプデでストーリーが完結したようです、全体を通して機械翻訳だったのでストーリーを読むモチベが生まれてこずあまり理解していませんが、祖父の借金返済の為に鉱石を掘っていたが、ひょんなことから祖父本人とアーティファクトの存在が絡み、また同じアーティファクトを狙う謎の組織が登場する...という感じでしょうか？
　今回のアプデでは新要素ではなくステージが1つ追加され、これまでと同様に惑星内に埋まった建造物を発掘して内部を簡単に調査する内容となっています。目新しさはあまりありませんが、鉱石を吸い取ってくれる”コレクター”のアップグレードがかなり良かったです。鉱石の吸収範囲を大幅に拡張でき、鉱石回収のテンポと気持ちよさが一気に向上しました。

This is one of the best $5 games I've played in a while, certainly this year. The Game About Digging a Hole was fun (and clearly a good idea) and may have started a "gold rush" of folks trying to cash in on similar things, but Digger: Galactic Treasures both elevates this concept to a higer level, and does so in pleasingly simple ways. Having to deal with gravity (especially in later levels) and oxygen, and the disorientation that happens in space adds a lot to this game while not over complicating it.

I love all the attention to detail and the clean art style. There's a lot to explore, from the stuff on the ship ([spoiler]and the minigames[/spoiler]), to the "secret" areas [spoiler]out in space[/spoiler]. The game does a good job creating a place and telling a story without just showing lots of text on the screen. Even the target ore for each level is something to be discovered, which is nice. Also cool that there's incentive to go back to earlier levels, not just to clear things out for OCD reasons (which I would probably do anyway), but also to [spoiler]get to areas that may have been inaccessible before[/spoiler].

The UI, controls and game mechanics all work really well. I like that we're basically alone, and there are no aliens/critters attacking. It has a nice chill vibe, and is one of those games where it's not player vs. enemy, or even player vs. environment, as much as player vs. themselves. The balancing feels really good too, with the tool progression and even oxygen levels not feeling so restrictive as to be frustrating, even in the earlier levels. That seems to be something missed by a lot of developers, so kudos on nailing that -- the game feels fair, if that makes sense.

Oh, and it does work on Steam Deck, at least docked and running at 1080p on a monitor -- that's what I've been playing it on. I turned the settings down a bit, and decided to use Medium since it made the fan run less. (Highest settings were a bit slow for me.) I also turned off motion blur, since I personally dislike it -- thanks for providing that as an option! The Low setting, at least on Steam Deck, changes the lighting enough that the light items become unnecessary since everything is well lit, even inside asteroids. It's kind of a nice option though, as it's a sort of "easy" mode, and the rest of the graphics still look good on Low. I was going to leave it on that until I noticed the lighting, which is why I changed to Medium. 

I don't really have any complaints or criticisms, but I think the weakest area in the game is probably the music. It's not bad, but if it was a bit more chill and hypnotic, it might make it easier to forget about oxygen levels and get into trouble. ;)

In any case, well done! This is a fun game at a fair price with enough original ideas to make it feel like something new, and something I'll happily play more of!

Digger: Galactic Treasures delivers exactly what it promises: a relaxed loop of [b]Dig, Sell, Upgrade, Repeat.[/b] You'll chip away at alien soil, guided by your trusty radar, hunting specific ores to meet each level's goal. Sell your haul, invest in better tools, and head back down. It's [i]simple, intuitive, and requires minimal thought[/i] – perfect for zoning out.

[b]The Good:[/b]

[b]Pure Relaxation:[/b] This is the game's biggest strength. It's [i]genuinely stress-free[/i], letting your brain rest. Just dig.

[b]Satisfying Progression:[/b] The [i]upgrade balance feels spot-on[/i]. Earning credits for better gear provides a clear, motivating goal.

[b]Visual Charm:[/b] While clearly a budget title, it [i]looks decent and has a pleasant, functional style[/i].

[b]Great Value:[/b] For its [i]low price[/i], offering around [i]5 hours[/i] of this specific grind feels fair.

[b]The Not-So-Good:[/b]

[b]Repetition is Key (and Flaw):[/b] The core loop [i]becomes very repetitive[/i]. Don't expect surprises.

[b]Lackluster World:[/b] The environments are [i]functional but ultimately pretty bland and boring[/i], missing a chance to add more visual interest.

[b]Forgettable Audio:[/b] The soundscape is mostly background noise, though the [i]warning signals (oxygen, full bag) are useful[/i].

[b]Thin Story:[/b] The intro has a touch of humor, but the plot is truly just [i]a flimsy backdrop[/i] and doesn't engage.

[b]Technically:[/b] I experienced only [i]minor, occasional frame dips[/i] when lots of small particles flew around, but nothing game-breaking. Solid performance overall.

[b]Who is it For?[/b]
This is [i]purely for players who enjoy a relaxed, almost meditative grind[/i]. If you like [i]chilling out with a podcast or music[/i] and making incremental progress without mental strain, Digger offers that niche experience effectively. It's [i]NOT for those seeking action, deep puzzles, or narrative[/i].

[b]Verdict:[/b] Digger: Galactic Treasures is a [i]competent, well-priced[/i] execution of a very specific, casual grind loop. It succeeds at being relaxing and offers decent progression. While the repetition and bland environments can lead to [i]bouts of boredom[/i] and it lacks broader appeal, it [i]delivers what it aims for[/i]. If "brain-off mining sim" sounds appealing, it's worth a look.

[b] 《Digger: Galactic Treasures》讲述的是在太空加州站的主角突然收到了一个噩耗，失踪一小时的祖父被找到，祖父被宣告死亡，主角继承了祖父的飞船以及债务，主角被剥夺了在太空加州站居住的权利被调往矿区，而在探索一个个挖矿星球的过程中主角逐渐收集装备和线索，发现了隐藏在背后的秘密——虚空之心 [/b]

[h2] 升级挖矿游戏 [/h2]
游戏的主要玩法就是玩家乘坐祖父的飞船借由公司的自动驾驶功能穿梭与一个个资源点之间，玩家需要完成公司要求的任务，通过探测器找到任务点挖取一定量的指定矿物才能前往下一个关卡。游戏目前提供七个地图，分为小型、银质、中型、大型四个行星和立方体、小型两个星球以及老旧的观测。关卡之间的资源从少变多，难度也变高，变成大型之后挖矿点会出现重力。

[h2] 膨胀很快的经济系统 [/h2]
员工挖矿获得的所有矿物没有所有权，一切矿物都归公司所有，但是玩家可以获得一定量的报仇，矿物从普通的金银铜铁到镍、泰坦、钛矿以及 各种宝石矿物，矿物还有一块大矿价格较高。玩家的经济在前期较为困难，但到了后期则较为膨胀。

[h2] 丰富的道具 [/h2]
游戏为玩家提供了丰富的道具为挖矿事业提供便利，由于之前飞船的物品全部被公司回收，所有的升级和道具都需要玩家购买，部分升级还需要玩家拾取特定道具解锁。游戏初始为玩家提供的挖矿工具是一把勺子，比较搞笑，玩家需要一勺一勺挖掘获取升级，在拾取到损坏的铲子之后可以升级为铲子加大挖掘范围，后续还能升级为铁镐。在拾取到冲击钻头可以升级为消耗能量的冲击钻，按住自动挖矿，有钱还可以买一个收集器，就不用手点矿物收集了。升级方面还为玩家提供了背包容量、炸药范围、飞行速度、氧气容量、扫描仪范围和电池容量升级。游戏还有一些便利的道具使用，如可以提供照明的便携灯光、一键回城的传送器、提供稳定供氧的空气发生器 。

 [h2] 游戏的不足 [/h2]
游戏的爽感和挖矿捡垃圾非常让人上头，但新鲜劲过去之后就会发现许多问题，游戏=的肝度较高，流程相对来说不算短但大部分时间肝的很无聊，汉化也有些问题，机翻、繁体字等问题很多，炸弹获取渠道过少，不能直接购买。好在游戏的售价相当便宜，推荐购入当一个打发时间的小游戏。

Again like a lot of things, I wish there was a middle ground instead of just a binary yay or nay.  But Let's do this.  There are some neat things.  A lot of potential.  Then an ending that was a rude whiplash moment that wholeheartedly earned the thumbs down.  Let's do the breakdown.

[h1]The Good[/h1]
This is a cheap game.  The run time is not long, but I played for 5.6 hours I think and I think I got my money's worth until the last minute of the game.  There was a lot of potential here.  I felt like it was a newer version of something like Hardspace: Shipbreaker.  The potential is there.  Build yourself up, pay your debt, keep trucking.  It was very chill and I didn't have to stress much.  I could see an end game potential where maybe you end up with some sort of generated systems, pay for a claim on one and go mine it for profit.  Was looking forward to where it was going to go.  There are tons of options in the game.  Do I want to drill, do I just want to blow things up?  Gives you options on how you wanted to tackle a situation.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]
The constant clicking of the mouse.  Now you can hold the button down to mine yes, but it mines at half the rate than if you were clicking.  How it could not be coded to simply mine fast by holding the mouse is beyond me.  Good quality of life option that should be in there.  The other annoying feature is that at the beginning of the game until you can get a larger oxygen capacity, you are stuck hearing that low oxygen error over and over and over.  Sure it is warning you and that is good, but you have so little oxygen at the beginning of the game, you sneeze and you are out of oxygen and hear the warning again.  At least give me a sexy voice to listen to if you are going to hit me with it again and again.

[h1]The Ugly[/h1]
The last few minutes of the game.  It was a fun and chill ride right up until that moment, and it was a big screw you from the dev(s) to us.  I found it jarring, rude, and plain just gave me whiplash.  I am not going to give a spoiler for it, but I was like..., "Wow I just wasted 6 hours of my life".  Everything I had done and built was literally for nothing, in a pre-scripted and pre-determined move that smacked of something a certain company that loves to make assassin games does.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I can't recommend this game.  There are some good things.  Lots of potential to maybe one day decorate your ship, get a different one, see some procedurally driven maps maybe.  But the way it was ended for me without any control or say on my part makes me give this a thumbs down.  Don't take my word for it though.  But you are gonna want to smack a goat at the end also.  Bad dev(s), bad.
